team1.notes: Strongest recommendation section in the class -- Chandler opened the deliberation correctly by calling for team consensus before anyone wrote a word, and the 30%-exemption / 2801-to-830 roster math is the clearest quantitative anchor any team used. Tyler Craig assembled the final document, edited Jason's section twice for tone, wrote conditions/next steps, coordinated the Google Doc link, and managed the submission timeline. That's a complete lead-author performance. Decision Rationale cross-references the Risk Matrix and Oversight Plan explicitly -- the document is building on its own prior work, which is exactly the assignment design intent. Significant process failure also on display: Jason Bogue required two coaching rounds (from Chandler and Tyler) to remove casual language from his section, and Brennan Monarch's first draft misread the entire prompt -- he wrote the risk of rejecting HarborRank rather than the risk of rejecting the team's recommendation to cancel. Brennan's corrected draft still hedges ('could,' 'might,' 'possibly') in a section that demands declarative language. The Risk if Not Acted Upon section is the weakest in the deliverable and the weakest across all three teams this week. No directed source used -- only team this week that didn't engage with additional sourcing.

team2.notes: The best section and the worst section of Team Y's WK14 are in the same document. Lindsey Allen's Decision Rationale is the strongest rationale section across all three teams -- specific guardrails named, EEOC liability stated precisely, cross-reference to governance plan SLAs, adverse impact monitoring required. If the rest of the memo matched that quality, this would be the top submission. It doesn't. Nathan's Recommendation opening paragraph is the weakest opening of any team: 'if the system manually screens high-volume applicate pools' reads as a conditional restatement, not a clear executive position. The 'five conditions' are referenced but not named in the opening paragraph. Risk if Not Acted Upon is thin -- connects to hiring targets and budget in general terms but doesn't quantify specific consequences. Harris: fifth consecutive week of non-participation. Nathan documented it in the status report ('Mekyle did not participate at all this week so I did his section'). Nathan's confidence rating of 8/10 with a specific evidence-based explanation for what would move it up or down is the most sophisticated reflection response of any team this week.

Haygood, Nathan.suggestedFeedback: You ran this week clean -- organized, followed up, assembled, submitted. Your confidence reflection in the SR (8/10, with specific evidence for moving it up or down) is the most analytically honest response any team wrote. The Recommendation opening needs work: 'if the system manually screens' reads as a condition, not a position. State it declaratively in the first sentence.
